ei.subject: 2025년 6월 고3 모의고사
ei.title: Laura and Cathy at the Farmer's Market

fullPassage:
(A) "Hi! I'm over here!" shouted Laura, waving brightly at Cathy at the entrance of Darlingdale Farmer's Market. Seeing her friend, Cathy rushed over in delight. Cathy had recently moved into Laura's town, and this was going to be (a) her first experience at a real farmer's market. Born and raised in a big city, where large supermarkets were more common, Cathy had never had a chance to buy freshly-picked fruits or vegetables.

(B) Carrying the bags of peaches, Cathy came back and noticed Laura holding a box of blueberries and jars of jam. "Cathy, those peaches look delicious! I bought some blueberries. Would you like to go to my place and make blueberry pancakes together?" Laura asked. "Yes, that's an excellent idea!" replied Cathy happily. As they walked out of the market, Cathy thanked her friend for the special experience, saying "(b) I really love this place! Thank you for the wonderful day."

(C) Entering the market, Laura said, "Let me show you around. Are you ready?" Cathy answered excitedly, "Absolutely! I'm going to buy some fresh peaches!" The market was already crowded with people of all ages. "Cathy, you can taste the best of the season here," said Laura. Cathy smiled and began to look around. Meanwhile, Laura found some strawberry jam for sale. She walked over to buy some. Curious to explore more, Cathy said, "While (c) you're buying jam, I'll look around the market and get some peaches."

(D) Wandering away from Laura, Cathy began to search for peaches. Cathy walked past booths of fresh flowers and hand-made soaps, which smelled heavenly. From a fruit stand, (d) she picked out some beautiful, ripe peaches. The fruit seller told her, "Those peaches are a great choice because they're only here until this week. If you miss them now, (e) you'll have to wait another year for the season." Hearing that, Cathy said, "Oh, I'll get some more then! They're really cheap!" She bought two bags of peaches.

questions.passage: "Hi! I'm over here!" shouted Laura, ①<u>waving</u> brightly at Cathy at the entrance of Darlingdale Farmer's Market. Seeing her friend, Cathy rushed over in delight. Cathy had recently moved into Laura's town, and this was going to be her first experience at a real farmer's market. Born and ②<u>raised</u> in a big city, where large supermarkets ③<u>was</u> more common, Cathy had never had a chance to buy ④<u>freshly-picked</u> fruits or vegetables.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ was → were: 선행사 'supermarkets'(복수)를 받으므로 복수 동사 were.
det.analysis:
❌ ③ was → were: 선행사 supermarkets(복수) → 동사도 복수
✅ ① waving: 분사구문(동시동작) — 정상
❌ ② raised: Born and raised(태어나고 자란) — 과거분사 병렬 — 정상
❌ ④ freshly-picked: 복합형용사(부사+과거분사) — 정상
det.tip: 주어-동사 수 일치: supermarkets were (복수). supermarket was (단수)

questions.passage: Entering the market, Laura said, "Let me ①<u>show</u> you around." Cathy answered excitedly, "Absolutely! I'm going to buy some fresh peaches!" The market was already crowded with people of all ages. Cathy smiled and began ②<u>to look</u> around. Meanwhile, Laura found some strawberry jam for sale. She walked over to buy some. Curious ③<u>exploring</u> more, Cathy said, "While you're ④<u>buying</u> jam, I'll look around the market."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ exploring → to explore: 'Curious to explore'에서 형용사 뒤에 to부정사 필요.
det.analysis:
❌ ③ exploring → to explore: 형용사(curious) + to-V 구조. curious to V = ~하고 싶은 호기심에
✅ ① show: let + O + 동사원형(사역동사) — 정상
✅ ② to look: begin + to-V — 정상
✅ ④ buying: while + S + be + -ing(진행형) — 정상
det.tip: curious + to-V: ~하고 싶은 호기심에. 형용사 + to부정사 패턴 (eager to, ready to, willing to)

questions.passage: Wandering away from Laura, Cathy began to search for peaches. Cathy walked past booths of fresh flowers and hand-made soaps, ①<u>which</u> smelled heavenly. From a fruit stand, she picked out some beautiful, ripe peaches. The fruit seller told ②<u>her</u>, "Those peaches are a great choice because ③<u>they</u> are only here until this week. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ Heard → Hearing: 능동 의미의 분사구문. Cathy가 듣는 주체이므로 현재분사.
det.analysis:
❌ ④ Heard → Hearing: 능동(Cathy가 듣는 것)이므로 현재분사. Hearing that = 그 말을 듣고
✅ ① which: 관계대명사(계속적 용법) — soaps를 선행사로 수식 — 정상
✅ ② her: 간접목적어(told her) — 정상
✅ ③ they: peaches를 가리키는 대명사 — 정상
det.tip: 분사구문: 능동 → -ing(Hearing), 수동 → p.p.(Heard). 주어가 듣는 행위자 → Hearing

questions.passage: Carrying the bags of peaches, Cathy came back and noticed Laura ①<u>holding</u> a box of blueberries and jars of jam. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② said → saying: 분사구문으로 동시 동작 표현. 'thanked ... saying'이 원문 구조.
det.analysis:
❌ ② said → saying: 분사구문(동시동작). thanked her friend, saying ~ = 감사하며 ~라고 말했다
✅ ① holding: 지각동사(noticed) + 목적어 + 현재분사 — 정상
❌ ③ to buy: a chance to V(to부정사의 형용사적 용법) — 정상
❌ ④ where: 관계부사(a big city where ~) — 정상
det.tip: 분사구문(동시동작): V1, V2-ing. thanked her, saying = 감사하며 말했다

det.korean: 농산물 직거래 시장에서 갓 수확한(freshly-picked) 과일을 살 기회가 없었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ freshly-picked(갓 수확한): 원문 표현 — 농산물 직거래 시장의 핵심 특징
❌ ① frozen(냉동된): 시장과 무관, 대형마트 제품
❌ ② imported(수입된): 직거래 시장은 현지 생산이 특징
❌ ④ processed(가공된): 직거래 시장은 비가공 신선식품

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 지금 놓치면(miss) 내년 시즌까지 기다려야 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① miss(놓치다): 원문 — 지금 사지 않으면 기회를 놓침
❌ ② purchase(구매하다): 구매하면 기다릴 필요 없으므로 문맥 반대
❌ ③ dislike(싫어하다): 이미 '좋은 선택'이라 했으므로 부적합
❌ ④ store(저장하다): 과일 판매 문맥과 무관
det.tip: miss: 놓치다, 빠뜨리다. If you miss them = 그것들을 놓치면

questions.passage: Cathy had recently moved into Laura's town, and this was going to be her first experience at a real farmer's market. Born and raised in a big city, where large supermarkets were more common, Cathy had never had a chance to buy freshly-picked fruits or vegetables.
questions.stem:
위 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.

"Cathy는 이전에 농산물 직거래 시장에서 과일을 산 적이 있다."

det.korean: Cathy는 갓 수확한 과일을 살 기회가 없었다(had never had a chance). 따라서 F.
det.analysis:
✅ F: 'had never had a chance to buy freshly-picked fruits' — 한 번도 산 적 없음
❌ T: 'first experience'이므로 처음 — 이전 경험 없음
det.tip: had never had a chance = ~할 기회가 한 번도 없었다. 과거완료+never = 경험 부정

"Laura는 시장에서 딸기 잼을 발견하고 사러 갔다."

det.korean: Laura가 딸기 잼을 발견하고 사러 갔다(found some strawberry jam for sale. She walked over to buy some). T.
det.analysis:
✅ T: 원문 'Laura found some strawberry jam for sale. She walked over to buy some.' — 정확히 일치
❌ F: 원문과 일치하므로 부적절
det.tip: for sale: 판매용으로. walk over: 걸어가다. 딸기 잼 발견 → 사러 감

questions.passage: Carrying the bags of peaches, Cathy came back and noticed Laura holding a box of blueberries and jars of jam. "Would you like to go to my place and make blueberry pancakes together?" Laura asked. "Yes, that's an excellent idea!" replied Cathy happily.
questions.stem:
위 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.

"Laura는 Cathy에게 자기 집에서 블루베리 팬케이크를 만들자고 제안했다."

det.korean: Laura가 'Would you like to go to my place and make blueberry pancakes together?'라고 제안. T.
det.analysis:
✅ T: 원문에서 Laura가 직접 블루베리 팬케이크 제안 — 정확히 일치
❌ F: 원문과 일치하므로 부적절
det.tip: Would you like to ~? = ~하시겠어요? (제안 표현). go to my place = 우리 집에 가다

det.korean: 친구를 보고 급히 달려갔으므로 기쁨(delight)이 적절.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ delight(기쁨): 친구를 보고 rushed over — 기쁨의 감정
❌ ① confusion(혼란): 친구를 향해 달려가는 상황과 부적합
❌ ② anger(분노): 밝게 손 흔드는 Laura에 대한 반응으로 부적합
❌ ③ disappointment(실망): 첫 시장 경험을 기대하는 상황과 반대

questions.passage: Wandering away from Laura, Cathy began to search for peaches. Cathy walked past booths of fresh flowers and hand-made soaps, which smelled heavenly. questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 더 사겠다며 정말 싸다(cheap)고 말했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② cheap(싼): 더 사겠다는 말과 함께 가격 만족감 표현
❌ ① expensive(비싼): 더 사겠다는 반응과 모순
❌ ③ heavy(무거운): 구매 결정과 무관한 속성
❌ ④ rare(귀한): 문맥상 가능하나 '더 사겠다'와 직접 연결되는 건 가격
det.tip: cheap(싼)↔expensive(비싼): 추가 구매 의사 = 가격 만족의 표현

ch: Cathy는 농산물 직거래 시장에 자주 갔다.

det.korean: Cathy는 대도시에서 태어나고 자랐다(Born and raised in a big city).
det.analysis:

❌ ① recently moved = 최근 이사했으므로 오래 살지 않음
❌ ② Cathy가 Laura's town으로 이사한 것이지 반대 아님
❌ ④ 'had never had a chance' — 한 번도 간 적 없음
det.tip: Born and raised in = ~에서 태어나고 자란. recently moved into = 최근에 ~로 이사한

questions.stem: 다음 글에서 문법적으로 틀린 부분이 포함된 문장은?

det.korean: ③에서 can → could: 간접화법에서 시제 일치 필요. Laura said (that) Cathy could taste.
det.analysis:
❌ ③ can → could: 주절 said(과거) → 종속절도 과거 시제 일치(can → could)
✅ ① 정상: 과거완료(had moved) + 과거(was going to be)
❌ ② 정상: 분사구문(Born and raised) + 과거완료(had never had)
❌ ④ 정상: 형용사+to부정사(Curious to explore) + would + 동사원형
det.tip: 간접화법 시제 일치: said + can → said + could. 주절이 과거이면 종속절도 과거

(A) "Hi! I'm over here!" shouted Laura, waving brightly at Cathy at the entrance of Darlingdale Farmer's Market. Seeing her friend, Cathy rushed over in delight. Cathy had recently moved into Laura's town, and this was going to be her first experience at a real farmer's market. Born and raised in a big city, where large supermarkets were more common, Cathy had never had a chance to buy freshly-picked fruits or vegetables.

(C) Entering the market, Laura said, "Let me show you around." Cathy answered excitedly. The market was already crowded with people of all ages. Meanwhile, Laura found some strawberry jam for sale.

(D) Cathy walked past booths of fresh flowers and hand-made soaps. She picked out some beautiful, ripe peaches and bought two bags.

(B) Cathy came back and they walked out of the market. Cathy thanked her friend for the special experience, saying "I really love this place! Thank you for the wonderful day."

Cathy, who had never visited a farmer's market, had a __________ first experience thanks to her friend Laura.

det.korean: Laura 덕분에 농산물 시장을 처음 방문한 Cathy가 즐거운(delightful) 경험을 했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① delightful(즐거운): 'rushed over in delight', 'wonderful day' — 긍정적 경험
❌ ② disappointing(실망스러운): 감사를 표현했으므로 실망과 반대
❌ ③ confusing(혼란스러운): 즐거운 경험이므로 부적합
❌ ④ exhausting(지치는): 감사와 기쁨을 표현했으므로 부적합
det.tip: 요약 문제: 글 전체의 감정 흐름(delight → excitement → gratitude)을 종합 판단
